## Body

All of PRDs 006-010 are live (#347 merged at 7b250e72; #355 flips 010 req-06 and ws 010 s04 with the receipt).

What #347's review (BLOCK, 6 findings) taught:
- A brake must never treat "could not read" as "nothing to do". A failed show, malformed JSON or an unreadable template means refuse, with an explicit override that is logged even when the input is missing. The same rule holds on both sides: shim and daemon.
- A cached "step done" is not proof now. Before accepting a recorded run step, re-run its live done check. Replay nothing and keep decisions. Clear the run after success, so the next cycle under the same key starts fresh (key pod-<pod>).
- Copying a folder that users fill: use entry.file_type() (does not follow links), canonicalize, and check containment against the template folder BEFORE reading. Refuse by path, never by content. Governance is public.
- Export pruning: drop every slot reference to a dropped slot (wiring, stage_needs AND not_model_of). Do the prune before json!(): json! serialises a copy.
- Shipped templates have no folder: show answers close_procedure.template null, and the shim runs repo or skill procedures (area `pods`).
- Criteria must match receipts. Take the receipt in the criterion's exact shape (008 req-09 needed 2 slots plus a consulted role). Don't weaken wording to fit a smaller measurement. Writer commits (git/ddocs) count as spawns, so say "no seat launch beyond the named writer commits".
- File targets (`--into` / `--as-template /tmp/...`) give a clean receipt with no governance residue. Delete the targets by exact path afterwards.
- Route budgets are fixed (pm-001): use pointers (`pij docs get pods`), not text. Merge bullets before asking for lines.
- Seeds (`--focus`) are not parameter-filled, so don't put <subject> in a slot seed. Slot `parameters` force the role to declare them.
- Biome reformats template JSON, so re-pin the hash after `biome --write`. In this test, the hash regex had to allow whitespace inside the tuple.
